cards.text: By the seventh month, the Israelites have settled in their towns, and the people gather in Jerusalem “as one man”. A whole crowd moving like ONE guy, friend, and the dead batteries I shared a junk drawer with couldn't even agree on who had the most charge left!

Two leaders step up: Jeshua son of Jozadak with his fellow priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel with his associates. They're ready to sacrifice burnt offerings to the God of Israel, just like it's written in the Law of Moses.

cards.question: Jeshua and Zerubbabel are ready to offer burnt offerings to the God of Israel. So what do they start building first?

cards.text: They set the altar up on its foundation, and the burnt offerings to the LORD begin, morning and evening. But something is hanging over all of it.

cards.question: The Israelites keep the morning and evening burnt offerings going, even though they ___ the people of the land.

cards.text: Next on the calendar, they celebrate a feast, just like it's written. And friend, when God's calendar says feast, you do NOT hit snooze!

cards.question: The Israelites celebrate a feast, just like it's written. Which feast is it?
During the Feast of Tabernacles, the Israelites offer burnt offerings every day, following the number prescribed for each day.

cards.text: After that, the altar gets a FULL schedule: the regular burnt offerings, the New Moons, all the appointed sacred feasts of the LORD, plus every freewill offering people bring. That altar's got a busier calendar than my ovens, and friend, my ovens are BUSY.

cards.question: When the Israelites start offering burnt offerings on the first day of the seventh month, the foundation of the temple of the LORD has already been laid.

cards.text: Now it's time to build. They pay the masons and carpenters, and they send food, drink and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre to bring cedar logs from Lebanon.

cards.question: The cedar logs from Lebanon make their way to Joppa by ___.
This whole cedar shipment happens with the go-ahead of Cyrus, king of Persia.

cards.text: In the second month of the second year after they arrived at the house of God in Jerusalem, the work begins. Zerubbabel, Jeshua, the priests, the Levites and everyone back from captivity: all hands on deck!

cards.question: The work on the house of the LORD needs supervisors. Who do Zerubbabel and Jeshua appoint?

answers.text: Levites twenty years old and up
Builders hired from Tyre and Sidon

cards.text: So Levite families team up to oversee the workers: Jeshua the Levite, a different Jeshua from the priest, with his sons and brothers, plus Kadmiel's family and the sons of Henadad. Nothing makes you lay a stone straighter than a supervisor standing right behind you!
And then it happens: the builders lay the foundation of the temple of the LORD. A FOUNDATION, friend, an actual FOUNDATION!

cards.question: To praise the LORD, the priests take their positions with ___, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, come with ___.
The priests and Levites praise the LORD the way ___ king of Israel had prescribed.

cards.text: They sing back and forth with praise and thanksgiving to the LORD: “For He is good; for His loving devotion to Israel endures forever.”

cards.question: The priests and Levites sing their praise and thanksgiving to the LORD. What do all the people do next?

answers.text: Give a great shout of praise
Head home to their own towns

cards.text: Now listen close, friend. Not every sound in that crowd is a cheer.

cards.question: Some in the crowd weep loudly when they see the foundation of this temple. Who are they?

answers.text: Older leaders who had seen the first temple
Young workers who had hauled the cedar
Persian officials who had come along

cards.question: While those older leaders weep, many others in the crowd shout joyfully.
With the weeping and the shouting going on at once, what can't the people do?

answers.text: Tell the shouts of joy from the weeping
See the foundation through the crowd
Finish singing the song they started

cards.question: The sound of that crowd is heard from far away.

cards.text: And that's where we'll set this batch down for now, friend. Only the foundation's in, and this story is FAR from done.
